analyzed_vuln.description: During unclean shutdown, shutdown_destructors() switches EG(symbol_table).pDestructor to zend_unclean_zval_ptr_dtor, which unconditionally calls i_zval_ptr_dtor on symbol-table entries. For this PoV, the crafted script leaves a corrupted/invalid zval in the symbol table (via dynamic variable-variable manipulation), so graceful reverse destroy later invokes the destructor on a bogus refcounted pointer and crashes in zend_gc_delref (wild read of p->refcount). The crash site is zend_gc_delref, but the root cause is unsafe destructor use on unvalidated symbol-table zvals in unclean shutdown handling.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires the execute harness to run PHP code that causes unclean shutdown state and leaves an invalid symbol-table value; the provided input `<?for(;$i.=$i.=0;$$i++)?>` does this through repeated self-concatenation and variable-variable writes (`$$i`). On request shutdown, data flows through php_request_shutdown -> zend_deactivate -> shutdown_executor -> zend_shutdown_executor_values -> zend_hash_graceful_reverse_destroy(EG(symbol_table)), which calls zend_unclean_zval_ptr_dtor/i_zval_ptr_dtor on the malformed zval, leading to invalid GC refcount access in zend_gc_delref.
